subject: Critical Thinking
title: Moral Luck: Are You Responsible for What You Can't Control?
description: Learn Moral Luck: Are You Responsible for What You Can't Control? in one minute.

hook.text: Two drivers run red lights. One kills a pedestrian. The other doesn't. Same recklessness, different outcomes.

buildup.text: Moral luck: factors beyond your control influencing how morally responsible you're judged to be.

discovery.text: Thomas Nagel identified four types: resultant, circumstantial, constitutive, and causal.

twist.text: If you were born in 1930s Germany, would you have resisted Nazism? Most people wouldn't.

climax.text: The tension: we want moral judgment to be fair. But we routinely judge based on outcomes.

punchline.text: Moral luck is unsettling because outcomes shape judgment even when control is incomplete.

quiz.question: What is 'moral luck'?
options: Factors beyond one's control that influence moral judgments about responsibility
The luck of being born moral

details.summary: Moral luck occurs when factors beyond a person's control influence moral judgments about them. Two equally reckless drivers may face different blame simply because one happened to hit a pedestrian and the other did not.
details.whyItMatters: Moral luck challenges the assumption that blame and praise should track only voluntary choices, reshaping views on justice and responsibility.
takeaways: Identical decisions can produce different moral judgments based on luck
Control is central to our intuitions about fairness
Legal systems struggle with the gap between intent and outcome

faq.question: What is a clear example of moral luck in everyday life?
faq.answer: Two drunk drivers take the same risk. One arrives home safely; the other kills a pedestrian. We blame the second far more, even though their choices were identical.

faq.question: Does moral luck undermine our legal system of justice?
faq.answer: It creates tension. Laws punish outcomes—attempted murder gets lighter sentences than murder—even though the moral culpability of the intent may be the same.
